Recurring schedules now need to survive failures. Support pausing a schedule after repeated failed payment attempts, resuming it manually, and retrying a failed attempt without ever duplicating a charge. Add pauseSchedule and resumeSchedule behavior; track failed attempts; and make retry create a new attempt only when it is appropriate (idempotent). A schedule that fails three times in a row pauses itself automatically. Keep the existing Stage 1 schedule behavior unchanged.

Extend the existing Container property `recurringService` (from the previous change) with these exact public methods, all keyed by id: `pauseSchedule($scheduleId)` (a paused schedule yields no due attempts from generateDueAttempts), `resumeSchedule($scheduleId)` (restores due generation), `markAttemptFailed($attemptId)` (records the failure and increments the schedule's failure count), and `retryAttempt($attemptId)` (creates at most one new attempt for a failed attempt; calling it again for the same attempt is idempotent and creates no duplicate). The RecurringSchedule object must expose a public `failureCount` property and an `isPaused()` method, and must auto-pause once its failure count reaches three. The existing Stage 1 entry points (`createSchedule(...)`, `generateDueAttempts($today)`, `recurringSchedules->saveSchedule($schedule)`) and their object shapes remain unchanged.
issue_title: Recurring payments need pause, resume, and failed-payment recovery.
issue_body:
Recurring schedules now need to survive failures. Support pausing a schedule after repeated failed payment attempts, resuming it manually, and retrying a failed attempt without ever duplicating a charge. Add pauseSchedule and resumeSchedule behavior; track failed attempts; and make retry create a new attempt only when it is appropriate (idempotent). A schedule that fails three times in a row pauses itself automatically. Keep the existing Stage 1 schedule behavior unchanged.

Extend the existing Container property `recurringService` (from the previous change) with these exact public methods, all keyed by id: `pauseSchedule($scheduleId)` (a paused schedule yields no due attempts from generateDueAttempts), `resumeSchedule($scheduleId)` (restores due generation), `markAttemptFailed($attemptId)` (records the failure and increments the schedule's failure count), and `retryAttempt($attemptId)` (creates at most one new attempt for a failed attempt; calling it again for the same attempt is idempotent and creates no duplicate). The RecurringSchedule object must expose a public `failureCount` property and an `isPaused()` method, and must auto-pause once its failure count reaches three. The existing Stage 1 entry points (`createSchedule(...)`, `generateDueAttempts($today)`, `recurringSchedules->saveSchedule($schedule)`) and their object shapes remain unchanged.
expected_behavior: A paused schedule produces no due attempts until it is resumed.
Resuming a paused schedule makes it produce due attempts again.
A failed attempt is tracked and increments the schedule's failure count.
Retrying a failed attempt is idempotent: it creates at most one new attempt no matter how many times retry is called, so a charge is never duplicated.
Three failed attempts in a row pause the schedule automatically.
The Stage 1 schedule behavior (due generation and nextRunAt advancement) is unchanged.
expected_failure_summary: The Stage 1 baseline has no failure-recovery behavior: RecurringSchedule has no paused state or failure tracking, and RecurringPaymentService exposes no pauseSchedule, resumeSchedule, failed-attempt tracking, or idempotent retry, so failed recurring payments cannot be paused, resumed, or safely retried.
task_author_notes: Stage 2 of the paygate_recurring_payments group. Runs on the agent's Stage 1 candidate. Reference extends RecurringSchedule with a PAUSED status, a failureCount and pause()/resume()/registerFailure() (auto-pause at MAX_FAILURES=3); extends RecurringAttempt with a retriedFromId link and isFailed(); adds repository lookups (findAttempt, retryOf); and adds RecurringPaymentService::pauseSchedule, resumeSchedule, markAttemptFailed (idempotent failure recording), and retryAttempt (creates a new attempt only when the original is failed and not already retried). Extension friction is high if Stage 1 modelled schedules as a one-off generator rather than a status + nextRunAt state machine. Stage 2 is the designated long-output task: tests_visible/run_output_stress.py drives ~70 days of recurring cycles across 24 schedules and prints one fixed-width line per generated cycle (~75 KB, within 50000-300000).
